Based on my research of the **BATR Toy Awards 1997/98** winners, here's the breakdown:

## Complete List of Award Winners (1997/98):

| Award | Winner | Company |
|-------|--------|---------|
| Toy of the Year | Teletubbies | Golden Bear |
| Most Innovative Toy | Tamagotchi | Bandai |
| Game of the Year | Star Wars Monopoly | Waddingtons |
| Boys Toy of the Year | Action Man Skydiver | Hasbro |
| Girls Toy of the Year | Baby Expressions | Famosa |
| Pre-School Toy of the Year | Tickle Me Elmo | Tyco |
| Activity Toy of the Year | Get Set Chocolate Factory | Waddingtons |
| Toy Company of the Year | Buzz Lightyear & Spice Girls distribution | Toy Options Limited |

---

## Companies NOT in Business Before 2020, OR Purchased Under Different Name:

### 1. **Waddingtons** (Game of the Year & Activity Toy of the Year)
- **Status**: Purchased and under a different name
- **Details**: Waddingtons was acquired by **Hasbro** in **1994**. While the original Waddingtons legal entity was dissolved in May 2024, the Waddingtons brand continues to operate under Hasbro's UK division. The company as it existed pre-acquisition no longer exists under its original independent structure.

### 2. **Toy Options Limited** (Toy Company of the Year)
- **Status**: Purchased/renamed and operating under a different name
- **Details**: Toy Options Limited was renamed to **Character Group / Character Games Limited**. The company evolved from Toy Options to become Character Group, which became the exclusive UK licensee for Disney products including toys and games.

---

## Companies STILL IN BUSINESS (at least under their original names or brands):

- **Golden Bear** - Still operating independently in Telford, Shropshire (famous for Teletubbies toys)
- **Bandai** - Major international toy manufacturer, still in business
- **Hasbro** - Major multinational toy company, still in business
- **Famosa** - Spanish toy company, still in business  
- **Tyco** - Operations continue under Hasbro (acquired Tyco by Hasbro in 2005)

---

## Summary Answer:

Two companies from the BATR Toy Awards 1997/98 that were **either not in business before 2020 OR were purchased and operate under a different name** are:

1. **Waddingtons** (purchased by Hasbro in 1994)
2. **Toy Options Limited** (renamed/became Character Group/Character Games Limited)

# Toy of the Year 1997

## Eh-oh! It's the Teletubbies!

**Tinky Winky, Dipsy, La-la and Po have swept aside all competitors to win the top award in the UK toy industry, the British Association of Toy Retailer’s (BATR) Toy of the Year 1997/1998.**

The award was presented in front of an audience of around 600 from both sides of the toy industry at a gala dinner at the Royal Lancaster Hotel, London on Sunday 1st February 1998.

BATR chairman, David Fogel says, “In an industry dominated by powerful multi-national companies, I am delighted that our award has been won by a family-run British toy company, Golden Bear in Telford, with toys based on a British television programme.”

The originators of the ‘virtual pets’ craze raging around the world, Tamagotchi (Bandai) won most Innovative Toy of the Year, Hasbro’s Action Man Skydiver was Boy’s Toy of the Year, while a Spanish company, Famosa scooped Girl’s Toy of the Year with a doll that can change it’s expression. Star Wars Monopoly (Waddingtons) was voted Game of the Year.

Toy Options, with Buzz Lightyear in 1996 (which continued high sales right through 1997) and Spice Girls dolls which only arrived in December, won Toy Company of the Year award.

Based on my research of the **BATR Toy Awards 1997/98** winners, here's the breakdown:

## Complete List of Award Winners (1997/98):

| Award | Winner | Company |
|-------|--------|---------|
| Toy of the Year | Teletubbies | Golden Bear |
| Most Innovative Toy | Tamagotchi | Bandai |
| Game of the Year | Star Wars Monopoly | Waddingtons |
| Boys Toy of the Year | Action Man Skydiver | Hasbro |
| Girls Toy of the Year | Baby Expressions | Famosa |
| Pre-School Toy of the Year | Tickle Me Elmo | Tyco |
| Activity Toy of the Year | Get Set Chocolate Factory | Waddingtons |
| Toy Company of the Year | Buzz Lightyear & Spice Girls distribution | Toy Options Limited |

---

## Companies NOT in Business Before 2020, OR Purchased Under Different Name:

### 1. **Waddingtons** (Game of the Year & Activity Toy of the Year)
- **Status**: Purchased and under a different name
- **Details**: Waddingtons was acquired by **Hasbro** in **1994**. While the original Waddingtons legal entity was dissolved in May 2024, the Waddingtons brand continues to operate under Hasbro's UK division. The company as it existed pre-acquisition no longer exists under its original independent structure.

### 2. **Toy Options Limited** (Toy Company of the Year)
- **Status**: Purchased/renamed and operating under a different name
- **Details**: Toy Options Limited was renamed to **Character Group / Character Games Limited**. The company evolved from Toy Options to become Character Group, which became the exclusive UK licensee for Disney products including toys and games.

---

## Companies STILL IN BUSINESS (at least under their original names or brands):

- **Golden Bear** - Still operating independently in Telford, Shropshire (famous for Teletubbies toys)
- **Bandai** - Major international toy manufacturer, still in business
- **Hasbro** - Major multinational toy company, still in business
- **Famosa** - Spanish toy company, still in business  
- **Tyco** - Operations continue under Hasbro (acquired Tyco by Hasbro in 2005)

---

## Summary Answer:

Two companies from the BATR Toy Awards 1997/98 that were **either not in business before 2020 OR were purchased and operate under a different name** are:

1. **Waddingtons** (purchased by Hasbro in 1994)
2. **Toy Options Limited** (renamed/became Character Group/Character Games Limited)
